{"table": "ANALYTICS.MARTS.DIM_REGION", "description": "One row per BEN_RES_REG code, with its label.", "columns": [{"name": "BEN_RES_REG", "type": "INTEGER", "description": "Code entier, clé de la dimension (une ligne par code, 14 valeurs distinctes, aucun nul), libellé dans BEN_RES_REG_LIB. Le nom évoque la région de résidence du bénéficiaire."}, {"name": "BEN_RES_REG_LIB", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Libellé du code BEN_RES_REG (vraisemblablement la région de résidence du bénéficiaire), issu d'une seed. 14 valeurs distinctes, une par code, sans aucune valeur nulle."}]}

content.text: Now I understand the data structure. The question asks for regions where the prescribing professional practices (PRE_INS_REG), and we need the statutory share reimbursed by Health Insurance for claims processed in March 2025. Let me query this:

input.sql:
SELECT 
  PRE_INS_REG,
  FLX_ANN_MOI,
  SUM(PRS_REM_MNT) as total_reimbursement
FROM ANALYTICS.MARTS.FCT_REIMBURSEMENTS
WHERE FLX_ANN_MOI = 202503  -- March 2025
  AND PRE_INS_REG != 99  -- Leaving out the unknown region (99)
GROUP BY PRE_INS_REG, FLX_ANN_MOI
ORDER BY total_reimbursement DESC
LIMIT 20;

content.text: Good! Now I need to get the region names. Let me check if there's a mapping between PRE_INS_REG codes and region names. Looking at the DIM_REGION table, it maps BEN_RES_REG to labels. Let me check if the same mapping applies to PRE_INS_REG:

input.sql:
SELECT 
  PRE_INS_REG,
  SUM(PRS_REM_MNT) as total_reimbursement
FROM ANALYTICS.MARTS.FCT_REIMBURSEMENTS
WHERE FLX_ANN_MOI = 202503
  AND PRE_INS_REG != 99
GROUP BY PRE_INS_REG
ORDER BY total_reimbursement DESC
LIMIT 3;

content.text: Now I need to get the region names for these codes. Let me check what region codes we have in the DIM_REGION table and see if we can use those labels:

content.content: {"columns": ["BEN_RES_REG", "BEN_RES_REG_LIB"], "rows": [[5, "Régions et Départements d'outre-mer"], [11, "Ile-de-France"], [24, "Centre-Val de Loire"], [27, "Bourgogne-Franche-Comté"], [28, "Normandie"], [32, "Hauts-de-France - Nord-Pas-de-Calais-Picardie"], [44, "Grand Est"], [52, "Pays de la Loire"], [53, "Bretagne"], [75, "Aquitaine-Limousin-Poitou-Charentes"], [76, "Languedoc-Roussillon-Midi-Pyrénées"], [84, "Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes"], [93, "Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur et Corse"], [99, "Inconnu"]], "truncated": false}

content.text: Perfect! Now I can join the region information with the reimbursement data. Let me create the final query:

input.sql:
SELECT 
  dr.BEN_RES_REG_LIB as region_name,
  SUM(fr.PRS_REM_MNT) as statutory_share_reimbursed
FROM ANALYTICS.MARTS.FCT_REIMBURSEMENTS fr
LEFT JOIN ANALYTICS.MARTS.DIM_REGION dr ON fr.PRE_INS_REG = dr.BEN_RES_REG
WHERE fr.FLX_ANN_MOI = 202503
  AND fr.PRE_INS_REG != 99
GROUP BY dr.BEN_RES_REG_LIB
ORDER BY statutory_share_reimbursed DESC
LIMIT 3;

Perfect! I have the answer. The three regions where the prescribing professional practises with the highest statutory share reimbursed by Health Insurance for claims processed in March 2025, excluding the unknown region (99), are:

1. Ile-de-France: 19978997.78
2. Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur et Corse: 18449445.53
3. Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes: 15638617.67
